subtopic: TVM / TensorIR schedule primitives — split, bind, cache_read
learningObjective: Reason about the effect of individual TensorIR schedule primitives on the resulting loop structure and buffer accesses.
stem: You have a TensorIR PrimFunc computing `C = A + B` with a single loop `for i in range(N)`. Which of the following schedule sequences are consistent with the semantics of TensorIR schedule primitives? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `sch.vectorize(loop=i)` is guaranteed to succeed on any loop regardless of the loop's extent, alignment, or the underlying target; TensorIR will silently emit scalar code if vectorization is impossible.

`sch.bind(loop=i, thread_axis='threadIdx.x')` may be applied without any prior split; this is a valid legalization that turns a single serial loop into a per-thread compute where each thread handles one element and blockDim is set to the loop's extent.

`sch.split(loop=i, factors=[None, 256])` produces two nested loops `(io, ii)` with `ii` size 256 and `io` size `ceildiv(N, 256)`; then `sch.bind(io, 'blockIdx.x')` and `sch.bind(ii, 'threadIdx.x')` map the two loops to the CUDA launch grid, producing a canonical vector-add kernel.

`sch.cache_read(block='C', read_buffer_index=0, storage_scope='shared')` inserts a shared-memory staging buffer between the load of `A` and its use in the C block, without changing the mathematical result.

explanation: A: `split` + `bind` is the canonical GPU schedule for a 1-D loop. B: `cache_read` inserts an intermediate buffer at the given storage scope, preserving compute semantics. C is wrong: `vectorize` requires the loop extent to divide the target vector width (and no cross-iteration dependencies); it may fail with an explicit error, not silently downgrade. D: `bind` directly on a 1-D loop is legal — the loop extent becomes the thread count. This is common for simple element-wise kernels; whether it is efficient is a separate concern.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: `vectorize` is not universally applicable; it errors when preconditions fail.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: `bind` on a single loop is legal legalization.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: `cache_read` inserts a scoped staging buffer.

assumptions: Standard TensorIR schedule primitive semantics as documented.
The reader is thinking of Unity-era TensorIR (not the pre-Unity TE `create_schedule` API).
nonImplications: Does not imply every valid schedule is performant; correctness and performance are separate.
Does not imply that `cache_read` always improves performance; it may hurt for tiny buffers.
